intent: These are NovaSeq reads downloaded from SRA (adapters already removed by the submitter). Remove the artefactual poly-G tails that two-colour chemistry puts at the end of short fragments, then write the cleaned reads.
silent_error: fastp trims poly-G tails by default only when it recognises Illumina NextSeq/NovaSeq data, which it infers from the original instrument-style read names. SRA-style headers (@SRR...) are not recognised, so poly-G trimming silently stays off and the G tails (called with high quality, so no quality filter touches them) pass straight through. -g/--trim_poly_g forces it. The run exits 0 and the log never mentions poly-G.
